ir_definition: "the imbalance ratio (the number of instances of the majority class for each instance of the minority class)"

outcome.smote_name_as_printed: ESM (Ensemble, SMOTE: "SMOTE in each iteration until 50% of the data belongs to minority class"); fixed-rate variants ESM100/ESM200/ESM500 also reported

chosen.table: Supplementary Table 11 (Geometric Mean, Boosting family) for RB-B and best_other; Supplementary Table 3 (Geometric Mean, Data-processing family) for ESM; RB-B values also in main Table 7, p.10-11
chosen.classifier: J48 (C4.5) unpruned, no collapsing, Laplace smoothing (C4.4), ensemble size 100
chosen.condition: 5x2-fold stratified CV, original datasets, ensemble size 100, default fusion (weighted average for RB-B, average for ESM)

summary_rows.label: Avg rank G-mean within family (main Table 10; RB-B in (c) Boosting family of 9, ESM in (a) Data-processing family of 11, not comparable rankings)
Hochberg adjusted p vs family best (Table 10; RB-B vs RUSB; ESM vs E-RB)

outcome.stat_test: Average ranks with Friedman / Iman-Davenport test, Hochberg post hoc test (within each family; across family-best methods in Table 13)

win_claim.quote: Experiments with 86 imbalanced data sets from two well known repositories demonstrate the advantage of the Random Balance approach.

uncertain: No single-classifier plain SMOTE exists; ESM is an ensemble of 100 J48 trees each trained on SMOTE-balanced data (no bagging/boosting). Treated as plain-SMOTE configuration; ESM100/200/500 are alternatives (Table 4, p.9).
Proposed (RB-B) and SMOTE (ESM) values come from different supplementary tables (Boosting vs Data-processing family), same protocol (5x2 CV, J48, size 100).
HDDT datasets how_obtained set to not stated: paper does not say which are natively binary vs binarised (p.6).
n_features left null: paper prints only (numeric/nominal) counts, kept in how_obtained_detail (Tables 2-3, p.7-8).
KEEL pima, haberman, wisconsin marked original, other KEEL repository-defined, based on KEEL naming only (p.8).
Exponent minus signs lost in text extraction for p-values (e.g. 3.0550e004), p.11-12.
Supplementary and main tables truncate long names (e.g. keel glass-0-1-2-3 vs 4-5 = glass-0-1-2-3_vs_4-5-6; keel ecoli-0-1-4-7 vs 2-3 = ecoli-0-1-4-7_vs_2-3-5-6; keel led7digit-0-2-4-5-6-).
notes: Proposed main method RB-Boost (RB-B, Random Balance + AdaBoost.M2); other proposed variants E-RB (Ensemble-RB) and BAG-RB (Bagging-RB). Main Table 7 gives only the three proposed methods per dataset (AUC, F-Measure, G-mean); all baselines per dataset are in the Supplementary PDF (Tables 1-22, AUC/F/G-mean/accuracy per family, plus fusion rules and base classifiers J48/SVM/KNN). SMOTE k=5. Boosting family SMOTE-related baselines are SMOTEBoost SB100/200/500 (not plain SMOTE). best_other taken from the other 8 Boosting-family methods in Supplementary Table 11. No bold/underline marks in supplementary tables (no bold fonts). Supplementary page numbers are PDF page indices of the Supplementary file and match its printed footers.
